newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Brazil Q3 GDP no signal of higher rates.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Brazil Q3 GDP no signal of higher rates.

text.p: Investors should not see Brazil's upwardly revised third-quarter economic growth as a sign that interest rates will rise near term, said Ernest Brown, an economist at Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
Brazilian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew 6.5 percent between the third-quarter 1995 and the third-quarter 1996, much sharper than an expected 4.0 percent gain, Brown said.

Expansion in agriculture, services and industry added to the output figures last quarter. Consequently, overall GDP growth for 1996 should be 3.0 percent rather than Morgan Stanley's previous estimate of 2.4 percent, Brown said.

But excluding certain seasonal factors, "the actual level of output, in our estimation, was flat in the third quarter," he said. And actual output is contracting by 2.0 percent in the fourth quarter compared with the third.

"The likely scenario for the remainder of this year doesn't include a strong pull on the supply-side numbers," Brown said. "After the end of the first quarter, if recovery continues strong, the story could change," he added.
